result.topic_en: Using the digamma function ψ(t)=Γ'(t)/Γ(t) to evaluate integrals of the form ∫₀¹(x^{p-1}/(1-x) − r x^{q-1}/(1-x^r))dx, and from these, integrals multiplied by finite and infinite lacunary sums x^a + x^{ab} + x^{ab^2} + ….
result.transcription:
Add Ms a 94 18(24) (24)

1. Let
$\psi(t) = \frac{\Gamma'(t)}{\Gamma(t)} = \int_0^1 \frac{1-x^{t-1}}{1-x}\,dx - \gamma,$
where $t>0$ and $\gamma$ is the Eulerian constant; so that
(1) $\psi(t+1) = \psi(t) + \frac{1}{t}$;
(2) $\psi(1) = -\gamma$;
(3) and $\lim_{t\to\infty}\{\psi(t) - \log t\} = 0.$
Then we see that, if $p, q$ and $r$ are positive, then
(4) $\int_0^1 \left(\frac{x^{p-1}}{1-x} - \frac{r x^{q-1}}{1-x^r}\right)dx = \lim_{s\to 0}\int_0^1 \left\{x^{p-1}(1-x)^{s-1} - r^{1-s}x^{q-1}(1-x^r)^{s-1}\right\}dx$
$= \lim_{s\to 0}\left\{\frac{\Gamma(p)\Gamma(s)}{\Gamma(p+s)} - r^{-s}\frac{\Gamma(q/r)\Gamma(s)}{\Gamma(s+q/r)}\right\}$
$= \frac{\Gamma'(q/r)}{\Gamma(q/r)} - \frac{\Gamma'(p)}{\Gamma(p)} + \log r$
$= \psi(q/r) - \psi(p) + \log r.$
From this we deduce that
(5) $\int_0^1 \left(\frac{x^{c-1}}{1-x} - \frac{b x^{bc-1}}{1-x^b}\right)(x^a + x^{ab} + x^{ab^2} + x^{ab^3} + \cdots + x^{ab^n})\,dx$
$= \sum_{\nu=0}^{[-\nu=1-]{+n+}} \left\{\psi(ab^{\nu-1}+c) - \psi(ab^\nu+c) + \log b\right\}$
$= \psi(\frac{a}{b}+c) - \psi(ab^n+c) + (n+1)\log b$
provided that $a+c$, $a+bc$ and $b$ are all positive. Supposing that $b>1$ {+and making $n\to\infty$ in (5)+} we obtain
(6) $\int_0^1 \left(\frac{x^{c-1}}{1-x} - \frac{b x^{bc-1}}{1-x^b}\right)(x^a + x^{ab} + x^{ab^2} + x^{ab^3} + \cdots)\,dx$
$= \psi(\frac{a}{b}+c) - \log\frac{a}{b}$
provided that $b>1$ and $a+c$ and $a+bc$ are positive. For example
